title: Jimmy McCulloch is fired from Wings | 1977
content:
Jimmy McCulloch was fired from Wings on 9 August 1977.

The young guitarist had been something of a loose cannon since joining Wings in the summer of 1974. He frequently drank heavily, and had a propensity for self-sabotage and destruction. Among his infractions were an arrest in Nashville for reckless driving; the trashing of a winnebago in Palm Springs; and a night of drinking in Paris in with David Cassidy during which McCulloch fell and broke a finger, necessitating a delay to Wings’ US tour in 1976. The rest of the band were no strangers to hard living, but they mostly managed to remain on the right side of civility.

The breaking point came after a drinking session in Campbeltown, Scotland, on the night of 8 August. After returning to the farmhouse at Low Ranachan, he smashed crockery, broke the dishwasher, and threw food and sauces at the walls.

First on the scene in the morning was Denny Laine. He quickly went to High Park Farm to warn Paul McCartney. Given McCulloch’s track record, there was no doubt as to the culprit.

A furious McCartney went to McCulloch’s room, ordered him to leave the farm, and to never return. His departure from Wings was announced to the press in September, when McCulloch joined The Small Faces for a series of live performances.

I enjoyed playing with Wings and I learned a lot from Paul, but I felt it was time for a change and the ideal change for me was The Small Faces. They are old friends of mine whose music I have always enjoyed.
Jimmy McCulloch

The press statement from MPL contained quotations from McCartney and McCulloch which touched upon the tensions within Wings.

Jimmy has been playing some great guitar recently and it’s a pity he is leaving, but problems have been building up for quite a while now and so the rest of us are happy to carry on without him.
Paul McCartney
